messages:
maria: heads up — saw a spike where high-priority tenants got routed to the tiny-backup model repeatedly this morning. looks like probe TTL + header override interaction.
raj: ugh. any obvious cb triggers? do we have cb logs for those tenants?
alex: cb_error_rate was below threshold but we saw repeated 'route-mismatch' on the gateway -> fallback. think the probe TTL expired and affinity header was ignored for TTL windows.
maria: paste of a sample request flow: `POST /v1/generate` -> X-RW-Tenant: acme -> X-RW-Routing-Pref: lane=low-latency -> probe TTL=30s -> response served by tiny-backup
sam: can you paste the gateway rule that matches the lane? suspicious about header precedence in the route matcher.
maria: here — small snippet from our routing config: ```
- match:
    path: /v1/generate
    headers:
      X-RW-Routing-Pref: lane
  action: route_to: lane-low-latency
  fallback: backup-tiny
  probe_ttl: 30s
  preserve_headers_on_fallback: false
```
raj: aha — preserve_headers_on_fallback=false will drop the affinity header when we hand off to fallback, so subsequent probe windows won't prefer the original lane. that explains repeated fallback loop.
alex: changing preserve_headers_on_fallback to true might keep the tenant pinned to the preferred lane across TTL, but we should be careful — if backup didn't have capacity earlier it might still route back to backup and cause sticky failures.
jen: also worth noting the console rollout UI currently exposes probe_ttl but not the header-preserve flag. ops teams have been changing TTLs without realizing the header effect. we should add that flag to the rollout UX.
tess: for safety, we should detect 'route-mismatch' churn in telemetry and auto-relax TTL or escalate to canary. maybe a metric: fallback_stickiness_count per tenant.
ops-bot: alert: tenant acme fallback_spike > 10 in 5m window (investigate) :warning:
raj: proposal: 1) set preserve_headers_on_fallback=true for lane-pref routes 2) add fallback_stickiness_count to platform metrics 3) console: show header-preserve toggle in rollout modal 4) small canary to 5% before global change
maria: +1 on all, but add a safety CB change: if fallback_stickiness_count > 50 within 1h, temporarily increase circuit-breaker sensitivity for that tenant (lower cb_error_rate threshold) to protect infra.
alex: implementation note — when preserve_headers_on_fallback is true we need to let fallback respect header hints but still allow explicit header overrides from tenants (we already have tenant-supremacy rules). test plan: unit test route matcher, integration test with probe TTL 5s/30s/2m buckets.
sam: I'll work on the config patch and add the telemetry counter. want to coordinate canary timing with infra; cc @eng-oncall.
jen: filing a tiny console ticket to expose the toggle and add a tooltip: "Preserve routing headers across fallback handoffs (can cause stickiness)."
tess: also add a dashboard widget that shows per-lane fallback churn and top offenders, so SRE can triage before alerts.
maria: thanks — assigning tasks: sam=patch, raj=telemetry metric + alert rule, jen=console UI, alex=CB tweak + tests. will run canary tomorrow 10am PT.
ops-bot: deploy-plan created: canary 5% -> monitor fallback_stickiness_count, cb_trips. scheduled 10:00 PT tomorrow. :calendar:
